extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) staff processing supplemental examination requests
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners on conducting supplemental examination proceedings under 35 U.S.C. 257, including preparing the supplemental examination certificate and the Reasons for Substantial New Question (SNQ) determination, panel review, and procedures after conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely SNQ determination (three-month requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months after the filing date of a request for supplemental examination, the Office will determine whether a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) affecting any claim of the patent is raised by any of the items of information presented in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination will generally be limited to a review of the item(s) of information identified in the request as applied to the identified claim(s) of the patent. The determination will be based on the claims in effect at the time of the determination and will become a part of the official record of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare Supplemental Examination Certificate and Reasons Document
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a determination is made on whether the items of information raise an SNQ, the examiner will prepare (1) the Supplemental Examination Certificate and (2) the Reasons for Substantial New Question of Patentability Determination (the 'reasons document').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reasons document typically accompanies the supplemental examination certificate and explains, for each item of information, why the item does or does not raise an SNQ. Form paragraph 28.01 should be used as the heading for the reasons document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the Supplemental Examination Certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplemental examination certificate lists all items of information properly submitted as part of the supplemental examination request and states whether an SNQ affecting at least one claim of the patent is raised in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should not initial, sign and date the listing of the items of information (37 CFR 1.610(b)(2)); the certificate includes a citation to each properly submitted item. The certificate will be electronically issued, display the filing date, list each item properly submitted, and state whether the request raises an SNQ affecting at least one claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons document must explain why each item does or does not raise an SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: For each item of information, the reasons document should explain whether the item, as presented in the request, raises an SNQ and identify the claims affected, or explain why the item does not raise an SNQ and identify the claims not affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (1) statement that the item raises an SNQ and identification of claims; (2) where appropriate, statement that the item does not raise an SNQ and identification of claims; (3) a brief statement of the basis for the determination. Use form paragraphs 28.02 (no SNQ) and 28.03 (SNQ) as templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an item raises an SNQ – required explanatory elements (A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an item of information is determined to raise an SNQ, the reasons document should point out: (A) that the item raises an SNQ affecting specific claims; (B) the specific claim limitation(s) affected; (C) what the teaching(s) are and where in the item the teaching(s) are found; (D) why a reasonable examiner would consider the teaching(s) important to patentability of the specific claim(s); and (E) where appropriate, whether the item is prior art to specific patent claims and reasons why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the specific claims affected, recite specific claim limitations implicated, cite the exact portion of the item that discloses the teachings, explain the importance to a reasonable examiner, and discuss prior art status (issue/publication dates) and rationale when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an item does not raise an SNQ – recommended explanatory elements (optional C–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each item determined not to raise an SNQ, the reasons document should state that the item does not raise an SNQ affecting specific claims and recite the specific claim limitation(s) discussed; it may optionally include what the teachings are and where found; why a reasonable examiner would not consider them important (e.g., cumulative or not important); whether the item is available as prior art and reasons; and, if not prior art, a statement that the item does not raise any other issues of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When explaining why an item is not important, include reasons such as cumulativeness to previously considered teachings or that the teaching was previously considered. If an item is not deemed prior art, explain why and explicitly state it does not raise issues under 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, or 112 when applicable (example: foreign search report). Use form paragraph 28.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify claims for which SNQ is (or is not) raised with granularity
rubrics_metrics.description: If an item raises an SNQ for some but not all claims to which the item was applied, the reasons document should identify those claims for which an SNQ was not raised and briefly state the basis for that determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the SNQ is raised for an independent claim, it may serve as the basis for dependent claims that incorporate the independent claim's subject matter, provided the dependent claims were also requested to be examined. Form paragraph examples illustrate partial-claim findings (e.g., SNQ for claims 1–5 but not 6–10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Only one SNQ need be identified per identified claim
rubrics_metrics.description: For each identified claim, the examiner need only identify one SNQ (e.g., a teaching that would be important to a reasonable examiner when determining patentability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may rely upon a single identified SNQ as the basis for the determination for that claim; no need to enumerate multiple alternative SNQs for the same claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address prior citation bar issues (MPEP §2242 II.A) when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, the examiner should explain why an item of information that was cited in the record of the patent is barred by the guidelines set forth in MPEP § 2242, subsection II.A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an item cited in the patent file is found to be barred, provide the specific reasoning referencing MPEP §2242 II.A to justify why it is barred from consideration as raising an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain whether the teaching was previously considered or is presented 'in a new light'
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is not clear from the patent file or supplemental examination record whether a teaching was previously considered, the reasons document should include either (i) an explanation that the teaching was not previously considered or addressed in any prior examination or proceeding, or (ii) an explanation that the teaching, if previously considered, is presented in a new light or different way by arguments in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explanation supports a determination that the item raises an SNQ (or not) by establishing novelty of the concern or a novel presentation of earlier material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests limited to correction of factual information must be supported
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the request includes an item limited to the correction of factual information, the request should also include one or more additional item(s) of information (e.g., intervening references) that potentially provide evidence that patentability of the claims depends upon the factual information to be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If correction-only items are provided without additional supporting items, the examiner should explain that the correction does not raise an SNQ because no items were included that show patentability depends on the corrected fact. Examples illustrate scenarios with intervening references and how to explain whether the intervening reference raises an SNQ depending on whether the domestic benefit is corrected or deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review of preliminary determination
rubrics_metrics.description: After an examiner makes a preliminary determination, the examiner will prepare draft certificate and draft reasons document, inform their CRU Supervisory Patent Reexamination Specialist (SPRS), and convene a panel review conference to review the preliminary determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2271.01 for panel make-up. If conference confirms the examiner's preliminary determination, the Supplemental Examination Certificate is issued (published in IFW and viewable in Patent Center) and the reasons document will be labeled and signed by the examiner with two conferees initialing. If not confirmed, the examiner must reevaluate and modify drafts in accordance with conference agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use prescribed form paragraphs and complete bracketed fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs ¶28.01 (header), ¶28.02 (no SNQ), ¶28.03 (SNQ), and ¶28.04 (reexamination ordered pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 257) should be used in the Reasons document and related orders. Bracketed fields must be completed per guidance (e.g., identify item, claims, filing and issue dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes provide examples for how to designate items in bracket 1 (e.g., 'the Jones patent', 'the March 11, 2011 BigBoxStore sales receipt') and what to insert in other brackets (claims, dates, patent number). When a SNQ is found for only some claims, explain which claims are affected and which are not per the example in ¶28.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of determination — ordering reexamination when SNQ found
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner determines that an SNQ is raised by one or more items of information in the request, ex parte reexamination of the patent will be ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To order reexamination the examiner may use form PTO-2302 or include form paragraph 28.04 at the beginning of an initial Office action on the merits in the resulting reexamination proceeding. The order may refer to the reasons document created during supplemental examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of determination — no reexamination and fee refund when no SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: If the supplemental examination certificate indicates that no SNQ is raised by any of the items of information in the request, ex parte reexamination will not be ordered and the fee for reexamination ordered as a result of supplemental examination will be refunded in accordance with 37 CFR 1.610(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The electronically issued supplemental examination certificate will be published as an attachment to the patent and remain part of the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing, issuance, and public availability of certificate and reasons document
rubrics_metrics.description: After preparation, the Supplemental Examination Certificate and reasons document are referred to the CRU Legal Instrument Examiner for clerical processing; they are made of record in the electronic file, copies mailed to the patent owner, and the certificate is electronically issued and viewable in Patent Center within three months of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The electronically issued certificate will display the filing date, list each properly submitted item, state whether an SNQ affecting at least one claim is raised, and remain part of the public record. The reasons document will be labeled 'Reasons for SNQ Determination' in IFW and generally available at or shortly after the certificate issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules and standards applicable to resulting ex parte reexamination (exceptions and material-to-patentability standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any ex parte reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 will be conducted in accordance with §§ 1.530 through 1.570, except for enumerated exceptions: (1) the patent owner will not have the right to file a statement under §1.530; (2) reexamination may be conducted on the basis of any item of information as set forth in §1.605 (not limited to patents and printed publications); (3) issues beyond those raised by patents and printed publications may be considered and resolved; and (4) information material to patentability will be defined by §1.56(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read 'applicant' references in §1.56(b) as 'patent owner' in the context of supplemental examination and resulting ex parte reexamination. These exceptions broaden the scope of what may be considered in reexamination ordered from supplemental examination versus standard ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination concluding act — electronic publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental examination is concluded by the electronic publication of the certificate; the Office procedure after publication depends on whether the Office determines an SNQ affecting at least one claim is raised in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an SNQ is raised, ex parte reexamination will be ordered; if not, the certificate will be published and refund rules applied. The certificate remains in the public record and may be published as an attachment to the patent.
